title: Combining Subordinate Clauses with Multiple Subjects

sections.content: You know *miután*/*mielőtt* (Unit 1) and multi-subject narration with *míg* (Unit 4). Now combine them: *miután*/*mielőtt* subordinate clauses AND multiple subjects — named or collective — in the same sentence. This is exactly the kind of sentence you need to narrate how the Magyar tribes actually settled the basin, since it involves several different groups doing different things over several years.

items.spanish: Miután a magyarok elfoglalták az Alföldet, fokozatosan nyugat felé terjeszkedtek, mielőtt 900 körül a Dunántúlt is meghódították.
items.english: After the Magyars occupied the Great Plain, they gradually expanded westward, before conquering Transdanubia too around 900.

items.spanish: A szláv törzsek egy része ellenállt, míg mások behódoltak és adót fizettek, miután belátták, hogy nem tudják megállítani a magyarokat.
items.english: Some of the Slavic tribes resisted, while others submitted and paid tribute, after they realized they could not stop the Magyars.

items.spanish: Miután a magyarok 907-ben, a pozsonyi csatában legyőzték a bajor sereget, biztosították új hazájukat.
items.english: After the Magyars defeated the Bavarian army at the Battle of Pozsony in 907, they secured their new homeland.

sections.content: Notice the second example also reuses *míg* from Unit 4 — a good multi-subject historical paragraph often mixes all your tools: named or collective subjects with matching verb number, sequencing words, *míg* for simultaneity, and *miután*/*mielőtt* for cause and effect. You don't need every tool in every sentence, but you should be able to reach for any of them.
